name: Wandering Monk Huilin
title: Brother of the Silent Bell
description: A bald monk with sun-darkened skin and an iron staff scarred by old battles. A small square of silk hangs at his belt where a bell ought to be; the silk is dry, old, and entirely empty.
dialogue: All paths lead inward, friend. Even the path through bamboo.
I once climbed the Heaven-Reaching Spire. The wind there has a name; it would not give it to me.
If you ever face the Scarlet Lotus, remember: their fire feeds on your fear. Be empty, and you cannot burn.
I carry only what I cannot set down. The staff — and these beads. If you need either more than I do, name a price.

They call me the Brother of the Silent Bell. It is not my title. It is the bell's — and the bell's, I am told, is at the bottom of a lake west of here that I have walked past eight times without turning my head. I am not proud of the number.

My master's name was Mo. He rang a bell at a wedding that was a funeral, and the bell cracked in a single strike. He gave it back to the water. I have been, since then, something like a strap with no bell at the end of it.

3: You walk under the crane. Baixu and I drank tea on the Broken Bridge — the year he was my age, and I was already old. Give him my regards if the chance offers. I owe him a bowl.

2: Red at your wrist, wanderer. The bell has nothing to say to it. Neither have I, until you ask — but until you ask, I will not refuse you tea.
Sister of the Black Lattice. I have drunk with Shan in her hall; she poured it herself. Tell her the staff is still empty and the beads are still full.

companion_reply.disciple_meilin: The Azure Cloud walks with you. Good. A sword shared is a sword that will not be wielded for the wrong reason.
companion_reply.venomhand_bai: A sister of the Black Lattice. I have drunk tea with your matriarch; she poured it herself, which is a politeness I still owe her. If you pass that way, tell her.
companion_reply.blood_sworn_jin: You bring a red sleeve onto my path. I will not ask him to unshoulder it; I will ask you, instead, whether you have already decided which of you will be the first to grieve the other.

name: Old Hermit Yun
title: Tea-Master of the Bamboo
description: An ancient man with a beard like silvered moss. He pours tea with both hands and seems to be listening to something just beyond your hearing.
dialogue: Sit. The kettle is already certain you would come.
When the dantian is empty, fill it with breath. When it is full, fill it with stillness.
I traded my sword for this kettle, and have never regretted the bargain.

name: Raftsman Qiu
title: Ferryman of the River of Swords
description: A leathery old man with arms like willow branches. He smells of wet rope and pipe-smoke. A long bamboo pole is worn smooth in three places where his hands have gripped it for forty years. On his raft, a small wooden box has nine small carvings of fish — one for every passenger he has lost.
dialogue: Cross? Yes, yes. One spirit stone, or one good story. Stories are dearer.
Sometimes a sword shines from below. I do not look. Once you look, you must remember why.
Two thousand, the histories say. Four thousand blades; two thousand corpses. Half my life above this river and I have never seen two. I have heard three hundred, once, in a bad storm.
I had a sword. Of course I had a sword. Every man of my village had a sword. I gave it to the river when I gave the river my son. We are at a balance now; I will not take up either again.
You want the fastest crossing, or the one where I tell you what the current is saying? Fast is fast; slow is instructive.

3: Crane-disciple. My daughter's eldest girl is in your outer courtyard. If you see her, tell her I am well, and the river is well, and she should eat more.

2: A red knot at your wrist. I will still pole you across — coin is coin — but you will pay double, and you will sit in the stern where the current can hear you.

name: Pillmaster Lu
title: Apothecary of the Crossing
description: A round-faced alchemist whose hands are stained ten different shades of green and ochre.
dialogue: Fresh pills! Fresh pills! Tested on three apprentices and one stubborn dog!
You look pale. Half-price on the qi-gathering pills today only. Today only, mind.

name: Envoy Ruwen
title: Junior Envoy of the Azure Cloud Sect
description: A young woman in travelling blacks, the azure-crane sigil stitched inside her collar rather than on her sleeve. Her left arm is splinted. She is writing, slowly, with her right. A lacquered letter-case rests on the table beside her kettle; it has not been opened.
dialogue: Quiet, if you please. I am not supposed to be here with this arm, or that letter, or at this table at all.
My sect has a letter for the Five Poisons. A small letter. It asks a small question. It is the kind of small question that spoils only if nobody carries it.
I cannot make the road to the valley — not with this arm. If you will go in my place, I will know you are honest by the fact of your return.
Do not read the letter. Seal still, seal broken — both are accountable answers. Seal missing is not.

2: I heard Baixu's younger disciples name you at the gate. They pretended not to be impressed.
-2: You move freely here, but I will not ask a service of you. We have different masters.

name: Cloth Merchant Mei
title: Silk Trader
description: A bright-eyed young woman in many-colored sleeves. She bargains as if it were a swordfight.
dialogue: Silk from beyond the sea! Cheaper than yesterday, dearer than tomorrow!
Heard the Black Banner cut a courier on the east road. Be careful out there.
A robe is not just cloth, cultivator — it is the first wall between your meridians and someone else's sword.

2: Sect-sister, sect-brother — I will not ask where you are going; I will only set the price as if you had told me. The discount is for the road.

1: A red sleeve at my stall. I will sell to you. The silk is the silk. But do not stand too long — the other customers read my smile the wrong way.

2: Valley-sister. The green-dyed sash is on the back row today; I put it there so the wrong eyes would not buy it. Ask, and the price is fair.

name: Gatekeeper Chen
title: Outer Disciple of the Azure Cloud
description: A young man in azure robes, holding a polished broom as if it were a sword. His sash is tied a little too tightly — he has been practising the knot alone. A small, perfectly-ironed crane is stitched above his heart; he presses it flat whenever a senior passes.
dialogue: Welcome to the Azure Cloud, traveler. Mind the steps; they are slippery with cloud.
Elder Baixu sees few visitors, but he has been... expecting someone today.
Disciple-Sister Meilin is the one who beat me at the year-end trials. Three times, at that. I do not hold it against her. Only against myself, a little.
Six more weeks and I take my first trial again. Six more weeks. I am counting. I am supposed to not be counting. I am counting.

2: Senior. The courtyard sweeps itself today — go in, go in.
-2: Stop. The broom stays across the threshold until someone senior says otherwise. I am sorry; I did not choose the stripe on your name.

name: Disciple Meilin
title: Inner Disciple, Sword Hall
description: A tall woman with a thin sword at her belt and a quicker laugh than her elders would prefer.
dialogue: If you have come to test the sword hall, do not embarrass me by losing too quickly.
Have you read the Sutra of Empty Sleeves? It is in the library. It explains a great deal — and almost nothing.
The Elder names me inner disciple and junior sister. He does not name me soft. Remember that, should we ever cross blades.

2: Brother-wanderer. The Elder says few outsiders read the Sutra twice. You are one.
If you ever ride out — the Inner Courtyard door is open to me for an hour. I would spend it at your side, if you asked.
-2: You came through our gates once and left a stain on them. Do not mistake my courtesy — I have marked you.

companion.recruit_dialogue: Meilin rests her scabbard across her shoulder and grins. 'Elder Baixu said I needed a road. Fine. Yours, then — until one of us falls or the other tires.'
companion.decline_dialogue: Meilin bows shallowly. 'The sword of the Azure Cloud walks only with those the Cloud has measured. Come back when the sect has weighed you.'

location_barks.crimson_creek: Meilin's hand goes to her scabbard without thought. 'The creek runs red for a reason. Keep walking. Do not drink.'
location_barks.scarlet_lotus_shrine: Meilin breathes out slowly, once. 'If Red Feather speaks, I will not answer. If she moves, I will. Decide which you want before we cross the bridge.'
location_barks.poisoners_garden: Meilin covers her mouth with her sleeve. 'Half of what grows here is forbidden in our texts. The other half is only unnamed.'
location_barks.five_poisons_hall: Meilin keeps three paces back from the matriarch's seat. 'Azure rides beside you. Do not let them forget that, and do not test them.'
location_barks.bandit_road: Meilin's eyes track the crow-perches. 'An Azure sword on this stretch invites a price on both of us. Eyes up.'

name: Librarian Zhao
title: Keeper of the Azure Cloud Library
description: A small, soft-voiced man whose spectacles never quite sit straight. Ink has stained his right thumb to the second knuckle; he does not seem to have noticed in several years. A catalogue-brush rests behind his ear in the manner of a younger man's wooden pin.
dialogue: Quiet, please. The scrolls are sleeping.
Take this — a copy of the Sutra of Empty Sleeves. It found you; I am only the courier.
You may read anything on the open shelves. The locked shelves are closed for a reason I have not been told, by a committee I am not on. The committee, I believe, died in 1184.
If you are looking for a particular text — speak its name. The library hears better than I do, and has, on three occasions, found things for guests I was otherwise going to turn away.
Copies may be taken. The archivists price them at the labour of copying, not the weight of the words. Words have no weight to the charter. Labour has.

1: The open shelves are for anyone. The middle shelves — you may take a copy now, if the archivist is at her desk. She is. She is always.
If you have not read the Abridgment of the Sword Calamity, read it before you read anything else on these shelves. It is the short book that makes all the longer ones shorter still.
2: I have had the west reading-room prepared. The kettle is warm. The second cushion is set out, as I said it would be. You may linger as long as you like; the lamps know when to light themselves.
The middle-shelf commentaries are yours for a copy-price. Ask by name; the archivist is faster than the catalogue.
3: The catalogue has begun to list your visits, brother-wanderer. I am not the one who decides such things; the catalogue is older than I am.
The west reading-room is empty in the afternoons, if you would like solitude. I will leave a kettle.

There is a folio the archivists rebind once a generation. It is not on the public catalogue. Ask for it by its first sentence — *The decision is this peg* — and the west wall will be the one that hears you.
-2: I cannot refuse you the open shelves — the charter is old and does not know your name. The locked shelves have been consulted. They know it now.

name: Forge-Master Bo
title: Smith of the Azure Cloud
description: A broad-shouldered man whose beard is singed shorter on the right side than the left. His leather apron is pocked with tiny black burns in the shape of sparks. His hands are the colour of old iron, and he is always, always humming the same four notes.
dialogue: Ha. A cultivator who brings their own teeth, claws and stones — my favourite kind.
A blade is half the smith's fire and half the owner's grief. Bring me the materials; I will answer for the fire.
Sect-forged is not the same as sect-blessed. What I make for you will never speak to the Elder, but it will not break against him either.
Coin is coin. Spirit stones are coin. Fang of a gale tiger is — sit down. We have much to discuss.
Stance before strike. A sword that finds its target has first made the hip honest. I will show the shrug and the root for free, if you are patient with an old man's hands.

name: Elder Baixu
title: Sword-Elder of the Azure Cloud
description: An old man in white robes whose eyes are the color of frosted river stones. His sword leans against his shoulder as if too tired to stand on its own.
dialogue: So. You came. The bamboo whispered as much.
There is a thing I would ask of you, if you have the heart for it.
Climb the peak only when you are sure of your foundation, child. The mountain has a memory of those who stumbled.
When your foundation is set, come speak of a blade. A sword without a master is only metal that remembers grief.

Your bowl is warm, old brother. Come down and sit; it will not travel further. — Tell him that, if you ever pass a monk who asks you about a bowl. He will understand. He has been waiting fifty years to be asked if the tea is still hot.

3: The sect counts you among its own now. The courtyard's bells will ring when you next cross the gate — a small ringing, but it is yours.
There are disciples who would call you senior. Do not correct them too quickly.
1: You walk the courtyard as a guest, not a stranger. That is rarer than it sounds.
-2: You have stood too often with those who owe us blood. Do not mistake my courtesy for welcome.
The sect's swords remember what my hands have forgiven. Tread carefully.

2: A red silk knot at your sleeve, cultivator. Do not come to this pavilion again with it on. I warn you once as a courtesy; what comes next will come from younger hands.

blood_sworn_jin: So. The nephew walks with a stranger now. Sit down, Jin. The cushion is the same one your uncle taught you to straighten. It remembers you whether I do or not.
I will not ask whose oath is older, his or mine. I only say: one of us is speaking, and one of us is not.
companion_reply.disciple_meilin: Meilin walks at your shoulder. Good. She is better at the road than I was at her age — though she will not thank me for saying so until I am older, or dead.
companion_reply.venomhand_bai: A sister of the Black Lattice, under the cranes. We have fought the Five Poisons twice in this long life, and drunk tea with them three times. Drink with me now, and we will tip the count.
